title: Multi-org validation - per-pod differences
intro: Two orgs on two pods, compared. Org A is an org on a dm-us pod; Org B is a sub-org on a dmp-us pod whose runtime environments are inherited from a parent org on the same pod. Org names, pod names, org and object IDs, host IPs and database names from the live runs are replaced with placeholders (<pod>, <orgIdV2>, <orgIdV3>, <parentOrgIdV3>, <agentId>, <reId>, <connId>, <private-ip>, <db>); every status code, count and verdict is kept exactly as observed.

blocks.title: The org under test
rows: <org> (Org B: a sub-org on a dmp-us pod)
The org that needed connections to an external application's PostgreSQL, MongoDB and ClickHouse stores.
The 22-char form. Use this for JWT X-INFA-ORG-ID and CAI URN paths.
The SAME org reports a different ID shape on the v2 plane. This is not a mismatch and not a bug — do not 'fix' it. v2 object IDs are prefixed with it (<orgIdV2>0B000000000002).
Org B is a sub-org. All four runtime environments are inherited from the parent, which is why they show zero agents.
Not dm-us. A one-character difference that silently 404s every borrowed URL.
Both planes share one base on this pod.
Includes Governance Owner, Governance Administrator, all four Data Marketplace roles, Customer 360 Manager and Data Steward, API Policy Manager, MDM Designer.
And yet CDGC, MDM, Marketplace and API Manager privileges are all present. Fresh proof that products[] is a licensing label, never the deployed feature set.
More than double the 153 seen on Org A (a dm-us pod). Connector catalogs are pod-specific.
An empty org — 1 auto-generated Project, no assets. So a 200-with-empty-list here proves the ROUTE exists; it says nothing about content.

blocks.title: Where Org A and Org B disagree
rows: Sub-orgs do not expose the license resource. Read entitlement from privileges instead.
Login audit is parent-org only. Use /api/v2/auditlog, which IS live on both.
GET /api/v2/dss, dtemplate, dmask, dreplicate, plan, fileListener
These v2 task resources mount per pod and per licensed engine, NOT per org. The single biggest source of false 'not entitled' calls.
Retested three ways. On dmp-us use the v2 form /api/v2/runtimeEnvironment, which returns 200 with all four REs.
GET /public/core/v3/agent, agentGroups, tags, licenses, orgs, permissions
The v3 admin surface is thinner on dmp-us than on dm-us. Same product, same month.
The anomaly below. Not a 404 and not a 401 — a route that answers and returns nothing.
1 registered (on the application's own cloud VM, v76.17, active=True, READY) as of 2026-07-26

SUPERSEDED 2026-07-26: the agent WAS installed on the application's cloud VM and registered into Org B. It reports exactly ONE engine, OpsInsightsDataCollector (Org A runs 17, incl. Data_Integration_Server), and packages=0. So no-agent is no longer the blocker - a SECOND, independent blocker sits behind it: no DI engine, so nothing agent-bound can OPEN a session. Connection DEFINITIONS still create fine (see the tables below).

blocks.title: What was ruled out, and how
rows: Wrong verb — v2 search is POST-shaped
Tried cdgc-api, idmc-api, <pod>-cdgc on dmp-us, plus cdgc-api.dm-us
idmc-api and cdgc-api on dmp-us: zero-byte 200. <pod>-cdgc: DNS failure. cdgc-api.dm-us: a clean 401 — proving the OTHER pod's route is real and merely rejects a foreign-org token.
Identical zero-byte 200 either way. A route that validated auth would differentiate.
Read effectivePrivileges: create.mcp.CatalogSourceConfiguration, create.PROFILE, execute.mcp.CatalogSourceConfiguration; roles Governance Owner + Governance Administrator
CDGC is licensed. Entitlement is NOT the explanation.
404 — so SOME data360 paths 404 while others zero-byte-200. The plane is partially mounted, which is the tell.

blocks.title: Host-derivation rule — how both of these were found
rows: CDQ dictionary API not mounted on this pod. The vendor's documented example uses a dm-us pod's -dqcloud-api host — pod-specific.
MDM host resolves but the B360 API is not mounted. Contrast the next row.
The unprefixed form does not exist. Always use <short>-.
Route exists, nothing behind it. Distinct from a 404 and worth re-probing later.
Wrong host family for Mass Ingestion.
The classic HTML-SPA false positive, on a NEW path. Confirms the base document's rule.

blocks.title: The verified request body
rows: The connector name. "PostgreSQL" and the shortName "PostgreSQLadapter" both return 403 APP_10519 'The connection type is not valid.'
TOOLKIT_CCI — the generic CCI toolkit type for every modern connector. The specific connector is named in instanceName, not here.
The DISPLAY string exactly as Administrator shows it — PostgreSQL. Matches the earlier S3-v2 lesson in this document.
hostName. Camel-case, and not the short form.
BOTH databaseName and database were present in the successful body. database was the last field the validator demanded.
Omitting it — it is not in most examples.
Read it from GET /api/v2/runtimeEnvironment. On Org B the Hosted Agent (<reId>) is the only RE usable without a Secure Agent.
Reusing databaseName / database, which is what PostgreSQL wanted.
MongoDB demands dbName specifically. With hostName + port + dbName the create returns 200. LIVE 2026-07-26: a MongoDB connection was created this way (<connId>, instanceName=MongoDB).
Assuming jdbcUrl alone is enough, or spelling it jdbcDriverClass.
Assuming jdbcUrl is the connection field.

JDBCV2 demands connectionstring TOO (same JDBC URL). It stores BOTH; a GET afterwards shows connectionstring + jdbcUrl and NO hostName/port/database - that is correct for JDBCV2, not a half-written record. LIVE 2026-07-26: a JDBCV2 connection to ClickHouse was created this way (<connId>).
There is no native ClickHouse connector in the 342-connector catalog.

Use instanceName=JDBCV2 (NOT JDBC_V2 or JDBC V2 - both return 403 'There is no connector with type='). The ClickHouse JDBC driver JAR must be present on the agent before the connection can actually open.

blocks.title: What this proves for connecting an external application's data stores to Org B
rows: Retrieve the Secure Agent install token + download URL
LIVE 2026-07-25. GET /api/v2/agent/installerInfo/linux64 -> 200 with a 122-char org-scoped install token + linux64 download URL.
Install + register the Secure Agent on the application's cloud VM

LIVE 2026-07-25/26. Installed as non-root user infa on the VM, installer checksum-verified (sha256), registered via consoleAgentManager.sh configureToken -> 'Login succeeded' -> getstatus READY. Agent <agentId> v76.17. Two blockers had to be cleared first, neither in the API: the cloud provider's firewall allowlist for SSH (:22) - the operator workstation egresses via a ROTATING corporate secure-web-gateway IP that changed mid-session - and an SSH key on the VM.
DONE - and it needed a real fix

A naive unit FAILS: infaagent resolves paths relative to its own dir, so ExecStart alone gives 'cannot open ./agent_start.sh' and the agent silently never starts after reboot. Requires WorkingDirectory=/home/infa/infaagent/apps/agentcore + RemainAfterExit=yes. Verified through a full systemctl restart -> active -> READY.
Create the connection (all three application data stores)

LIVE 2026-07-26, all POST /api/v2/connection -> 200, all bound to the same agent (<agentId>): a PostgreSQL connection (<private-ip>:5432/<db>), a MongoDB connection (<private-ip>:27017/<db>) and a JDBCV2 ClickHouse connection (jdbc:clickhouse://<private-ip>:8123/<db>), each with its own <connId>.
NO - blocked by the DI engine, NOT by the connector

LIVE 2026-07-26: GET /api/v2/connection/{id}/test -> 403 APP_105060 'Unable to resolve channel service. No running service found of type...' for ALL THREE. The definition is valid and persisted; there is no Data Integration runtime on the agent to open a DB session. This CORRECTS the older row that cited Org A's 2026-06-28 green tests - that was a different org with DI entitled and it does not transfer to Org B.
Run a catalog source / profile against it

Needs (a) a DI/CDGC engine on the agent and (b) the data360 zero-byte-200 anomaly resolved. Re-confirmed 2026-07-26: on Org B, /data360/search AND its deliberately-bogus sibling (/data360/search/api/v99/bogusZZZ) both return 200 with 0 bytes, as does /cdmp-marketplace/.../bogusZZZ -> gateway prefix routing, not a capability.

notes: The application's data plane is NOT on localhost. All three stores are Docker containers bound to the VM's PRIVATE IP (<private-ip>; postgres:16.13, clickhouse/clickhouse-server:25.3, mongo:7.0.31). Every localhost port is closed, so a connector built with hostName=localhost cannot work. Verified on-host 2026-07-26.
Data volume was production-scale (hundreds of millions of rows in the analytics store), so governance over it would not be vacuous.

The validator-iteration technique in the request-body table is the most reusable thing here: POST a partial body, read the ONE attribute named in 403 APP_105054, add it, repeat. It discovered dbName, jdbcdriverclassname and connectionstring - none of which appear in any local vendor PDF.

products[] on the Org B login still reads 'Integration Cloud' only, yet 876 privileges / 38 roles include Governance Owner. Reinforces the standing rule: products[] is a licensing label, never the deployed feature set. The DEPLOYED ENGINE LIST off the agent is the ground truth - and it is only readable once an agent exists, which is a new argument for installing one early.
open_questions: Does the parent org (<parentOrgIdV3>) own Data Integration + CDGC entitlement to allocate down to Org B? UNRESOLVED from the API: both available credential sets are the same Org B-scoped user, /api/v2/org returns only Org B with subOrgs=[] and subOrgLimit=0, and every license path is absent (/v3/licenses 404, /api/v2/license 404, /api/v2/org/{id} 403 REPO_10404). POST /api/v2/agent/service -> 500 CMN_001, matching the Org A row, so there is NO REST plane for engine enablement. Needs a parent-org admin in Administrator > Sub-Organizations > Licenses.
Once DI is entitled: does the JDBCV2/ClickHouse connection need its driver JAR staged manually on the agent, and where? Not yet attempted.

Connection credentials that reuse the database containers' own credentials (the POSTGRES_USER / CLICKHOUSE_USER from the container environment) are POC-only: replace them with least-privilege read-only database users before going further.
